Title: [Excerpt from] “A Feather Is a Letter from a Bird”
Author: by Susan Westley
Content: On `text(Monday)`, Jimmy ran along the sandy white beach.
Crunch, crunch. Shells broke beneath his sneakers.
Suddenly, Jimmy saw something sticking up from the sand. He bent down to pick up a velvety gray-and-white feather.
“A feather is a letter from a bird,” said Mom, walking up behind him.
“Read it to me, please,” Jimmy said, handing it to her.

“H'm, let me see.” Mom turned the feather over and upside down. “Ah, this is interesting: Dear Jimmy, I watched you build a sandcastle today. I'm a builder, too. I make my nest with grass and seaweed. Your friend, Laughing Gull.”
Jimmy and his mom looked up to see a gull sailing by. Jimmy waved.
On `text(Tuesday)`, Jimmy sat on the beach, digging a hole in the sand.
Jimmy looked up to see a brown bird dive into the water and come up with his beak billowing out like a large balloon.
A brown feather floated on top of `text(one)` foamy wave. Jimmy jumped up and waded into the water, then ran to Mom. “Another letter, Mom! Can you read it to me?”
“This is a pelican feather,” she said, turning the sandy brown feather over and upside down. “It says: Dear Jimmy, I eat fish. What do you like to eat? Your friend, Pelican.”
Jimmy laughed. “Let's fry fish tonight, Mom!”
On `text(Wednesday)`, the smell of shrimp, mussels, and fish floated through the air at the noisy farmers' market.
Jimmy stopped when he spied a long-legged white bird strolling along the sandy path nearby. A feather fell from its wing. He grabbed it before anyone could step on it.
“Mom, another letter from a bird!”
“Read it, read it, please!” Jimmy heard the tall bird squawk at people passing by.
“Dear Jimmy, I live in marshes, swamps, shorelines, mudflats, and ponds. Where do you live? Your friend, Snowy Egret.”

Early `text(Thursday)` morning, Jimmy and his mom strolled along the wooden boardwalk through the mangroves. They stopped on the bridge to watch a rose-colored bird swish her spoon-shaped beak back and forth in the water, searching for food. A misty feather floated through the air and landed at Jimmy's feet. His eyes grew big as he picked it up and handed it to Mom.

“This is lovely,” she said, turning the feather over and upside down. “Dear Jimmy, do you like my pale pink feathers? I get them from eating shrimp. Aren't I beautiful? Your friend, Roseate Spoonbill.”
On `text(Friday)`, Jimmy ran along the shoreline, dragging a stick behind him.

He began to carve marks into the sand. “Dear birds, I live in the white cottage near the shore. Did you see my house? I like pizza, but eat fish, too. Send me another letter soon. Your friend, Jimmy.”
Just then, Jimmy heard a twee-wee-wee and looked up to see a sandpiper skitter past him. In its wake was a brown-and-white speckled feather. Jimmy picked it up and ran to his mother.
